title: Motivation
examples: What is the difference between wanting to do something and needing to do it?
How does setting goals help my brain?
Can I use small wins to feel more motivated?

explain.say: Today we are learning about what keeps us motivated to learn.

items: Motivation is the reason for action.

explain.say: One type of motivation comes from inside yourself.
If you learn because you find it fun, that is intrinsic motivation.
Doing something for a reward is called extrinsic motivation.
Setting clear goals gives your motivation a direction to follow.
Achieving small wins builds momentum for bigger goals.

faq.q: What is the difference between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation?
faq.a: Intrinsic motivation comes from within you, like enjoying reading for fun. Extrinsic motivation comes from outside, like reading for a good grade.
asks: Is it internal or external motivation?
What is the difference between wanting to do something and needing to do it?

faq.q: How important are goals when I am trying to learn something new?
faq.a: Goals help you focus your energy and give you something to work towards. They break big tasks into manageable steps.
asks: How do goals help my brain?

faq.q: Are small wins really helpful for staying motivated?
faq.a: Yes, celebrating small wins gives you a feeling of success. This feeling makes you want to keep going with bigger tasks.
asks: Can I use small wins to feel more motivated?

faq.q: Does one type of motivation work better than the other?
faq.a: Neither is always better; they work together. Using both internal interest and external rewards can be effective.
asks: Which is better, inside or outside motivation?
Can I rely only on one type of motivation?

faq.q: If I only work for grades, am I being motivated?
faq.a: You are using extrinsic motivation in that case. Try to find some part of the subject you genuinely enjoy too.
asks: Is getting a good grade enough motivation?
What if I only care about the reward?

facts: Intrinsic motivation is driven by internal satisfaction.
Extrinsic motivation is driven by external rewards or pressures.
Setting goals provides focus and direction for effort.
Small wins build confidence and maintain momentum.

quiz.say: You study biology because you are genuinely curious about how cells work. This is an example of:
quiz.why: Intrinsic motivation comes from your own natural interest and curiosity.

wrong.1: This suggests an outside reward was the main reason for studying.
wrong.2: While goals are involved, the core reason stated is internal enjoyment.
wrong.3: This describes the result of studying, not the initial reason for it.

quiz.say: A student practices piano every day to earn praise from their parents. This is primarily:
quiz.why: The motivation here is linked to receiving praise, which is an external reward.

wrong.0: This refers to the planning, not the source of the drive.
wrong.1: This describes a small achievement, not the overall source of motivation.
wrong.3: This would mean the student practices because they love the sound of the music itself.

quiz.say: To keep working on a difficult essay, you break it into writing an introduction, then one body paragraph, and finally the conclusion. This strategy uses:
quiz.why: Breaking the task down and completing each part creates small, achievable successes.

wrong.0: Goal setting is the overall plan; small wins are the steps within that plan.
wrong.2: While you might feel intrinsic motivation, the technique described is structural.
wrong.3: This implies the small wins are only for external rewards, which is not the focus.
